about.title: About
about.lead: PropaGraph demonstrates fake news detection from propagation graphs with graph neural networks.
about.method: Each news item is a propagation tree: the root is the news, the other nodes are users who shared it, and edges are sharing relations. GNN models (GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN) learn a representation of the whole tree to predict real or fake, on the UPFD dataset (PolitiFact and GossipCop). The project asks three questions:
questions: How much does propagation structure contribute compared with content and user features?
Which feature types and architectures matter most?
How early can fake news be detected when only part of the tree is observed?
does: Browse sample propagation trees from PolitiFact and GossipCop.
Draw trees radially, coloured by time and sized by onward shares.
Predict real or fake with a probability using the trained GNN.
Simulate early detection with a time slider.
Show experimental results and data-reliability findings from the notebook.
doesNot: Accept new URLs or news text: UPFD has no source text and user features can no longer be re-collected.
about.course: Specialised project 2, class 23GITB, Vietnam-Korea University of Information and Communication Technology.
